MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 6, 2018

A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Zuckerman, Schmitz, Carman, Medawar,
  Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Buresh, Carrese, Corman,
  Friedman, Shinn, Silvano, Wagreich

  Committee Members Absent:  Portugal, Seamans, Stegura

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Sr. Planner Naughton

  Also present from Dyett & Bhatia:  Rajeev Bhatia, Elizabeth Blanton, Meghan McNulty

3.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

4.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

Items taken out of order

Planning Director Wahba stated that new to the City this year are Student Commissioners and
Committee Members who will be attending meetings and are welcomed to provide input. Planning
Director Wahba introduced Michael Wagreich from Peninsula High School as the GPAC’s Student
Committee Member.

  C. Project Status Update

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia, provided a brief update on the project and the next steps going
  forward.

  B. Key Themes from Existing Conditions Report
  i. Presentation
  ii. Discussion/comments on key themes and issues.

  Meghan McNulty, Dyett & Bhatia, provided a PowerPoint presentation on the key findings in
  the five chapters of the Existing Conditions Report.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that in regards to the presentations mention of approximately
  7% available land for development, it should be clarified that this is in one concentrated area
  of the City. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that in order to make good policy decisions, the

  1
GPAC Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2018
   following area should be further researched: 1) the number of equestrian users in the City; 2)
  air quality at a local level; and 3) travel information at a local level.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed her concerns on the instances in the report
  where findings and recommendations are in areas that are not under the City’s jurisdiction.

  Rajeev Bhatia stated that the General Plan will need to clearly show the City’s vision. In the
  case where other agencies are planning projects, there will be a clear understanding of what
  the City has envisioned.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that walking and cycling are not reasonable alternatives due to
  the City’s topography. Walking and cycling are more recreational than they are used for a
  means to commute.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO stated that developing more bike paths on the hill may
  draw people to the City.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated it is important to first identify areas in the City that
  need improvement, such as retail, recreational, and transportation. From a retail perspective,
  the business corridor has suffered and is in need of major improvement.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that she walks from the Bay Club to CVS on Silver
  Spur and it was not designed to encourage pedestrian traffic.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that a study was done years ago in order to make
  a pedestrian-friendly connection from the Peninsula Center to the Post Office. Within the plan
  there was also a shuttle as a way to connect all the businesses.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that for seniors who have limited mobility, this
  would be essential and would allow them to be more independent.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ added that this may also be a good alternative for other
  age groups including people with young children.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN expressed his concern on the expense of a shuttle
  service. He stated that a similar service was attempted in 2005 and again in 2010 with very
  low ridership.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that merchants may be interested in funding a
  shuttle service to the business corridor.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WAGREICH stated that among his age group, most places are in
  walking distance. Transportation by bus is an inconvenience and are more likely to opt for
  more convenient transportation.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that PV Transit is essentially a school bus. There must be
  thought given to realistic alternative transportation in the City.

  COMMITTEE SCHMITZ stated that there must be a distinction between the jurisdictions
  because it matters in policy decisions as well as cost.

  2
GPAC Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2018
   CHAIR ZUCKERMAN suggested that clarification is needed to the Office Inventory graph on
  page 44, 3-8 and the Rents and Vacancy graph on page 45.

  COMMIITTEE MEMBER SILVANO stated that equestrian should not be limited to equestrian
  users, there are people who enjoy the equestrian lifestyle unique to the City.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN stated that in Section 4 (Circulation), there are many maps
  but there are none showing the areas with the most congestion. For example, during certain
  periods of the day, there is heavy traffic on Palos Verdes Drive North.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested that due to the limited number of streets into
  the City, a program to commute children to and from school should be explored, and added
  that the two most congested areas are the commercial corridor and Palos Verdes Drive North.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WAGREICH stated that taking the bus is a negative experience.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BURESH asked if the landslide issues were considered when
  identifying Deep Valley Drive as a potential development site. Planning Director replied that
  there was a study done on the site and it was considered during the analysis of the site.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN suggested that a reference to the study be included and consideration
  be given to including hazard zones.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BURESH stated that the development of that site will be expensive
  and it is unfair to describe it as underutilized.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that something must be done about the hillside known as, “trash
  bag hill”.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ asked the following questions on behalf of COMMITTEE
  MEMBER STEGURA: 1) In section 6 (Landfill) there was no mention about waste diversion,
  will it be a part of the update?; 2) asked that the report clearly delineate that the Library is its
  own district; 3) stated that there were no educators interviewed for the stakeholder interviews
  and wanted to make sure that someone from the school board or educators are included in
  the interviews; 4) in regards to school traffic, what is the demographic?; 5) why no one
  complained about the lack of athletic fields.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER asked if there is any plan to update the current codes and
  stated that the current codes are being ignored by the residents as well as the enforcement
  officials (i.e. overnight parking). COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER asked about emergency
  preparedness. In addition, she asked how the stakeholder interviewees were selected.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that he attempted to get a cross-section of the community
  and also through public outreach. COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that she as well
  as other members of the CITY COUNCIL also contributed names for the list of interviewees.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN asked how privately owned businesses’ will be encouraged
  to make improvements.

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there need to be guidelines and enforcement for poor
  business signage.

  3
GPAC Meeting Minutes
February 6, 2018
   Planning Director Wahba asked if there is an interest to do a horse census and local air quality
  testing.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ asked that the horse census be added to the Emergency
  Preparedness section of the Policy Development Session agenda.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVANO stated that equestrians would be interested in a census,
  however, a license would not be well received.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that there are many implications in regards to traffic,
  including how to evacuate people from the hill in case of a major disaster.

  A. Overview of Public Outreach Strategies
  i.  Review of Draft Citywide Online Community Survey questions.  Ideas for
  additional questions.
  ii.  Ideas for locations and strategies for future “pop-up” meetings.

  Elizabeth Blanton, Dyett & Bhatia, provided an overview on public outreach strategies and a
  review of the survey questions that have been prepared.

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS contributed ideas on how to get the survey distributed, including:
  contacting HOA’s, Chamber of Commerce, School E-Daily Bulletin, and placing on Nextdoor.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN suggested adding a question to the survey in regards to
  promoting sustainability and adding a question to ascertain if there is any interest in having
  more pedestrian walkways.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested adding a statement on the approximate time it
  will take to complete the survey.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR asked if the survey will be limited to only residents.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that the survey will also be available to business owners.

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS agreed that the survey should be available for 30 days.

  Ms. Blanton stated that comments from the public will be taken on an on-going basis. The
  types of questions during various “pop-up” events will correlate with the stage of the project
  at that time.

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS contributed ideas on “pop-up” meeting sites, including: the Wine
  Walk at the Peninsula, Mayor’s Ride/Pancake Breakfast in May, City Celebration, School
  Registration Days, “Whale of a Day” event in March.

  Mr. Bhatia stated that the results from the survey will be compiled to be discussed at the next
  GPAC meeting.

5.  COMMITTEE REPORTS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  None

  None

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  CARRESE to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:02 PM.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.
